summary: Round 5, test review. F1, F2 and F3 verified fixed by measurement. 28 mutations of Lease.java applied and reverted individually; 24 killed, and every one of the 4 survivors is behaviour-equivalent or fail-closed, named below with the exact mutation. All 22 red records present and bound to the current LeaseTest sha256 (60fa27ee...), all re-recorded 2026-09-03. Full suite 454 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped. Tree restored, git diff clean, staged hash unchanged.

findings.title: The UPPER end of the control-character boundary is still unpinned: `c < 0x20` -> `c <= 0x20` survives all 22 tests
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED. Mutate Lease.java:107 `if (c == '"' || c == '\\' || c < 0x20)` to `c <= 0x20`; `./gradlew :format:test --tests binjava.format.LeaseTest` is green (exit 0). Under the mutant `new Lease(1, "pod 1", "e", 5L)` and `new Lease(1, "p", "host 1:80", 5L)` both throw, where the unmutated code accepts them and round-trips them correctly (verified against the compiled class). The hostile array now pins 0x00, 0x01, 0x0A and 0x1F -- every case is a REFUSAL, so nothing constrains where the refused set stops. F2 asked for both ends: the dangerous end is now closed (`c < 0x1F` dies on `pod\u001Fx`, confirmed), this is the fail-closed end. Consequence is a narrowed domain, not corruption: a K8s pod name cannot contain a space and an endpoint is host:port, so it is unreachable in M4.3b's use. Closing it costs one line -- assert `Lease.decode(new Lease(1, "pod 1", "a b", 5L).encode())` round-trips -- which would also pin the acceptance side of the guard the way the emoji/astral assertions pin the surrogate guard's.

findings.title: `expiresAtMillis < 0` -> `<= 0` survives; the epoch's twin boundary IS pinned, so the asymmetry is accidental
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED. Mutate the compact constructor's `if (expiresAtMillis < 0)` to `<= 0`: all 22 green. Under the mutant `new Lease(1, "p", "e", 0L)` throws where today it is accepted. The mirror mutation on the epoch (`epoch < 0` -> `epoch <= 0`) is KILLED by four tests, because `anEmptyHolderEndpointIsAcceptedBecauseM4HasNoPeerMeshToPublish` constructs epoch 0 -- no test constructs expiry 0. Fail-closed and practically unreachable (an expiry of 0 is a lease already expired at the epoch of the clock), so this is worth one value in an existing test, not a round.

findings.title: Both of `longField`'s guards are individually deletable with the suite green -- the same equivalent-mutant shape round 2 fixed in `stringField` by asserting the message
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED, two separate mutations, each green across all 22 tests. (a) Delete `if (at < 0) { throw new IOException("lease is missing " + name ...); }` from longField. (b) Change `if (end == from)` to `if (false)`. Both survive because the outcome is still an IOException by a different route: for (a) the canonical re-encoding always emits all four fields and so can never equal an input missing one, and for (b) `Long.parseLong("")` throws NumberFormatException which longField's own catch converts. So the contract that matters -- IOException, never an unchecked escape -- holds under both mutants, and the loss is diagnostic only (`lease is not in canonical form` / `lease has a malformed epoch` instead of `lease is missing epoch` / `lease has a non-numeric epoch`). Note the contrast: `stringField`'s identical `at < 0` guard IS killed, because `aLeaseMissingAStringFieldIsRefused` asserts `hasMessageContaining("missing holderPodId")`. Nothing decodes a lease with NO `epoch` or NO `expiresAtMillis` field at all -- `{}` exits through the shape/length path first -- so those two are the only guards in the file with no input reaching them. Two `hasMessageContaining` assertions would close it. Related and equivalent for the same reason: deleting `catch (NumberFormatException e) { throw new IOException(...) }` also survives, because NumberFormatException extends IllegalArgumentException and decode's outer catch already wraps it -- verified live, the mutant still throws IOException.

findings.title: The M4.3 row documents four rounds and then closes with "Three rounds, and every one found a real defect"
findings.failure_scenario: The row's last clause was written at round 3 and not updated when the round-4 paragraph was inserted above it, so a reader counting rounds from the summary sentence gets 3 where the body names 4. This is exactly the failure mode the M4.0 row names as its own durable lesson ("fixing ONE copy of a fact and missing its duplicates"), inside the row that records it. Honesty on the substantive point is fine: the row states plainly that round 3's own verdict named the character U+1D800 and that three files copied the error. No gate catches a stale count in prose.

verified: F1 (upper surrogate bound). MEASURED: `cp <= 0xDFFF` -> `cp < 0xDFFF` now dies, uniquely, on anUnpairedSurrogateIsRefusedThoughAValidAstralPairIsNot -- the round-4 MAJOR is closed. `cp >= 0xD800` -> `cp > 0xD800` also dies on the same test, so BOTH ends are pinned; deleting the whole surrogate guard dies too.

F2 (control-character lower bound). MEASURED: `c < 0x20` -> `c < 0x1F` now dies on aHolderFieldContainingJsonHostileCharactersIsRefused, via the added `pod\u001Fx` case. Deleting the guard entirely also dies. The opposite end survives -- filed as a minor above, as requested.

F3 (the U+1DC00 naming). ARITHMETIC VERIFIED: U+1DC00 - 0x10000 = 0xDC00, so the surrogate pair is 0xD837/0xDC00, matching the escape `\uD837\uDC00` in the test; its low 16 bits are 0xDC00, inside the surrogate range, so `(char)` truncation misclassifies it. U+1F600 truncates to 0xF600 (Private Use), confirming the emoji alone does not discriminate. `grep -rn '1D800'` over all .java and .md finds only the two deliberate 'not U+1D800' corrections in LeaseTest.java:299 and the backlog row; no copy still asserts the wrong name.

Red records. All 22 test methods in LeaseTest have an entry in .harness/tdd/red.json, every one carrying sha256 60fa27ee... which equals the current file, and every one timestamped 2026-09-03 -- i.e. re-recorded after the F1/F2/F3 edits, as claimed. Spot-checked as genuine independently: 18 distinct test methods were each observed to be the unique or joint killer of a real mutation in this review.

Individual discrimination after the edits. 24 of 28 mutations killed, and no test lost a unique killer to the hostile-array additions: `pod\u001Fx` and `pod\nx` were added INSIDE aHolderFieldContainingJsonHostileCharactersIsRefused, so they can only strengthen that one method, and the method it might have made redundant -- theFieldInjectionThatWouldFabricateAnExpiredLeaseIsImpossible -- was already a joint rather than unique killer of the quote guard before the edit (both die together on dropping `c == '"'`). Its value is the named attack, not a distinct mutant.

Silent-corruption class, the theme of all four rounds, searched exhaustively rather than by mutation. Encode side: UTF-8 is total and lossless over well-formed Java strings, so the only characters that survive `getBytes` non-identically are lone surrogates, and the only characters that can break the JSON structure or forge a field marker are `"` and `\` -- all four are refused and all four are tested. Verified `new Lease(1, "}:,{", "a b", 5L)` round-trips, so the guard is not wider than it needs to be. Decode side, probed against the compiled class: CESU-8 lone surrogate (ED A0 80) and an overlong quote (C0 A2) are both MalformedInputException; a UTF-8 BOM prefix, interior whitespace, and a trailing second object are all IOException. I could not construct an input that is accepted and means something other than what it says.

Tier and testing.md. T0 throughout -- no store, no socket, no clock (isExpiredAt takes the instant as a parameter, non-negotiable 7). No Thread.sleep, no fixed port, no system temp, no mock. All four staged files are additions or docs, so no existing assertion could have been weakened.
Suite. `./gradlew test`: 454 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped, aggregated from every module's test-results XML. Matches the claim.
Tree. Every mutation reverted; `git diff` empty, `git status` shows only the four staged paths, `git diff --cached | sha256sum` still a06609cd758c378fedf4606a115ea81f7a029aec2a0211ce175902a0cfe025a5.
